records.title: PHI/PII screen is still text-regex only: clinical narratives classify as non-sensitive, and image/PDF/document blocks are labelled 'unscreened_media' in the ledger but still dispatched
records.evidenceAtHead: No commits since 92ccdba1 touch server/services/ai-governance/classification/ or server/services/ai-gateway/pii-screen.ts or sensitive-placement-policy.ts (git log 92ccdba1..HEAD on those paths: empty). (1) heuristic-classifier.ts:33-48 has the same 7 detectors (ssn, email, credit_card, phone, labelled MRN, labelled DOB, labelled plan id); nothing for names, subject IDs or AE narratives. Command run: npx tsx scratch script classifying 'Subject 1001-023, Maria Gonzalez, a 54-year-old female, experienced a serious adverse event of hepatic failure on Day 14 and was hospitalized ... She died on 12 March 2026.' -> {"phi":false,"pii":false,"classes":["public"]}; positive control 'Contact jane@example.com' -> pii:true. (2) classification/index.ts:23 defaults AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE to heuristic; slm-classifier.ts:36-56 still falls back to the heuristic even when AI_CLASSIFIER_SLM_URL is set (stub). (3) pii-screen.ts:97-114 extractRequestText still reads only string content and type:'text' blocks ('Non-text blocks ... are not inspected'). (4) gateway.ts:1398-1413 maps that result to sensitiveDataClass 'none'; sensitive-placement-policy.ts:51 returns ALLOW_NON_SENSITIVE for 'none' before any zero-retention or approval check. (5) gateway.ts:4829-4843 ledgerDataClass (new since audit) only RECORDS 'unscreened_media' in the ledger; nothing refuses. (6) Media still reaches providers unscreened: routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1628-1675 (ANA_ENABLE_PDF_INTAKE=true; sends PDF and also text/plain files as base64 document blocks, so even plain-text uploads skip the screen) and AnaDocumentDraftingService.ts:900-935 analyzeImage (image block). Mitigations that landed since audit, not closing the finding: org-placement.ts (d29275b1b) limits production vendors to anthropic/bedrock/local unless elected; gateway.ts:4693-4705 requestPlacementDenial enforces an org-level zeroDataRetention election for every data class.
records.remaining: Entire finding: no detector for patient names, subject/randomisation IDs, age+sex+event narratives or dates of death/hospitalisation; no PHI-possible floor for clinical-document payloads; image, PDF and base64 document blocks are not inspected and not refused when the placement is not approved for PHI; the SLM classifier is an unimplemented seam. Only the ledger label is honest now ('unscreened_media').
records.severityRationale: A design-partner biotech will upload protocols, CSRs and SAE narratives through AnA and Authoring. Today those are classed 'none' and dispatched with no zero-retention or approval check. The production vendor default (Anthropic/Bedrock/local) and the per-org ZDR election reduce the exposure, so the pilot can start. The screen still has to be fixed, or the pilot org configured with zero_data_retention and the limitation written into the DPA, before pilot users rely on it for clinical content.
records.humanTestingNote: Not visible to testers. Classification is silent, and non-production defaults to audit mode, which never blocks. Testers must not upload real patient-identifying data on local or staging. If the fix below lands and staging runs AI_SENSITIVE_DATA_POLICY_MODE=enforce, AnA PDF/image requests will be refused until AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS grants the provider PHI/zero-retention approval. That refusal is expected.
records.instructions:
1. Failing-first tests. (a) Add server/services/ai-governance/classification/__tests__/clinical-narrative.test.ts asserting that HeuristicContentClassifier.classify() returns phi:true for: 'Subject 1001-023 ... 54-year-old female ... serious adverse event ... hospitalized ... died on 12 March 2026'; 'Patient 0042 (initials J.D.)'; 'randomization number R-10234'. Keep negative controls ('Study 1001 enrolled 240 subjects', plain ICH prose) at phi:false. Run it and confirm it FAILS at HEAD. (b) Add a gateway test, next to server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/governance-review.test.ts and using its governedGateway()/stubDispatch helpers, with NODE_ENV=production and AI_SENSITIVE_DATA_POLICY_MODE=enforce: a request whose only content is an image block, or a base64 application/pdf document block, sent to a provider whose AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS entry lacks zeroRetentionApproved must reject with GatewayPolicyError and dispatch nothing. Show it FAILS at HEAD.
2. In server/services/ai-governance/classification/heuristic-classifier.ts DETECTORS (lines 33-48), add phi-class detectors: subject/patient/participant/randomization identifiers (e.g. /\b(?:subject|patient|participant|pt|screening|randomi[sz]ation)\s*(?:id|no\.?|number|#)?\s*[:#]?\s*[A-Z]{0,3}\d{3,}(?:[-/]\d+)*\b/i), demographic narrative ('\d{1,3}-year-old (?:male|female|man|woman|boy|girl)'), and labelled dates of death, admission or hospitalisation. Keep each regex anchored to a label so regulatory prose does not false-positive. Update the module header to say what is covered.
3. In server/services/ai-gateway/pii-screen.ts extractRequestText (lines 102-114), also decode base64 document blocks whose media_type is text/plain and include their text. Export a new requestCarriesUnscreenedMedia(request) that returns true for image blocks, PDF/base64 document blocks, Files-API file blocks and request.imageContent. Move the media test out of gateway.ts ledgerDataClass (lines 4836-4843) into this function and have ledgerDataClass call it, so there is one implementation.
4. In gateway.ts route() classification (lines 1398-1413) and the embedding path (lines 1668-1682): when the text result is 'none' and requestCarriesUnscreenedMedia(request) is true, set sensitiveDataClass to 'phi' (PHI-possible) and record the basis 'unscreened_media' on the request and the ledger row. decideSensitivePlacement (sensitive-placement-policy.ts:47-) then requires a zero-retention-approved placement. Do NOT map it to 'unknown': that is DENY_DETECTOR_FAILURE and would misreport the reason.
5. Clinical-document floor: when payloadProvenance is 'tenant_governed' and the callerModule/taskType is a clinical drafting or analysis task (document_analysis, section generation, AnA attachment intake in routes/ana-ri/stream.ts:1628-1675), raise 'none' to 'phi'. Keep the list as an explicit const in pii-screen.ts with a comment that names each entry.
6. Leave AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE=slm documented as not implemented. In server/startup/ai-governance-posture.ts, refuse boot in production when AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE=slm, because slm-classifier.ts:52-55 silently uses the heuristic even with a URL set.
7. Re-run the step-1 tests and show they now pass. Run server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/tenant-capacity.test.ts and the existing classification tests to confirm no regressions.
8. Pilot operations (founder): until steps 2-5 land, set the pilot organization's placement policy to zero_data_retention=true, and set AI_PROVIDER_PLACEMENT_APPROVALS so that only a contracted ZDR Anthropic/Bedrock lane carries zeroRetentionApproved. gateway.ts:4693-4705 then enforces ZDR on every call regardless of class.
All commits go on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) The new classifier test fails at HEAD and passes after the change. The SAE narrative, subject ID and randomization examples classify phi:true; plain regulatory prose stays public. (b) The new gateway test fails at HEAD and passes after: in production+enforce, an image-only or PDF-only request to a provider without zero-retention approval rejects with GatewayPolicyError and nothing is dispatched; the same request to a ZDR-approved provider is served, and its ledger row shows data class phi with basis unscreened_media. (c) A text/plain attachment containing 'MRN: 12345678' is classified phi (its text is now screened). (d) Production boot refuses AI_CLASSIFIER_MODE=slm.
records.dependencies: AI-02 (a provisioned, high-risk-approved provider lane); a provider zero-data-retention contract so some placement can carry zeroRetentionApproved; AI-08 org placement defaults (landed in d29275b1b)

records.title: Metering and rate buckets now follow the bound tenant; per-process in-memory buckets, no token/cost cap and opt-in fail-open weekly limits remain
records.evidenceAtHead: Fixed parts: gateway.ts:4180-4186 recordTenantUsage now reads auditOrganizationId(request), which is the bound tenant (explicit or ambient, bindTenant gateway.ts:4718-4740). At 92ccdba1 it read request.organizationId only (gateway.ts:3905). policy.ts:108-132 rateBucketKey keys the bucket on sensitiveTenantPolicy.organizationId. At 92ccdba1 it was request.organizationId || '__global__' (policy.ts:520). gateway.ts ~3586-3615 refuseUnboundInProduction rejects production calls with no tenant before any bucket. Command run: npx vitest run server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/tenant-capacity.test.ts -> 9/9 passed, including 'one tenant's ambient-bound calls do not spend another tenant's rate budget'. governance-review.test.ts:308-330 covers ambient metering. Still open: policy.ts:259 rateBuckets is still a per-process Map; terraform/stack has api_desired_count but no Redis/ElastiCache (grep finds none), so the effective org limit is 100/min x task count. The never-checked dailyCost accumulator was deleted (grep dailyCost server -> none) rather than enforced, and no per-org token or cost cap exists anywhere in the gateway. bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:24 still wires only enforceWeeklyLimit('requests') on /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat. enforceWeeklyLimit.ts:113-122 still fails open by default. Weekly limits are opt-in per org. weekly-usage-limits.ts:37 supports cost_cents and tokens, but nothing enforces them. Editor AI, MCP and other gateway callers are not covered.
records.fixedBy: e2258d07a (2026-09-29, after 92ccdba1): server/services/ai-gateway/gateway.ts:4180-4186 (recordTenantUsage via auditOrganizationId), gateway.ts:4718-4740 (bindTenant), gateway.ts refuseUnboundInProduction; server/services/ai-gateway/policy.ts:108-132 (rateBucketKey) and removal of the unused dailyCost map
records.remaining: (1) Rate buckets are in-memory per process (policy.ts:259), so the limit multiplies with ECS task count and resets on deploy. (2) No per-organisation token or cost cap is enforced in the gateway, and none is applied by default per plan. (3) The weekly limit covers only /api/ana, /api/ana-ri and /api/chat, counts requests only, is opt-in, and fails open. Authoring editor AI (/api/c2c ai-editing), the MCP connector and job-driven calls are uncapped.
records.severityRationale: Attribution is correct now. Every bound call is metered to its org, and tenants no longer share a bucket. That removes the cross-tenant denial-of-service and the unbilled-usage exposure. For one invited, founder-supported pilot org, the remaining gaps are spend control and multi-instance precision, not safety or integrity. They need fixing before enterprise GA or self-serve plans.
records.humanTestingNote: Not observable in normal testing. A tester who drives a long AnA Auto turn plus heavy tool use above 100 gateway calls a minute for one org on one process gets 'Organization rate limit exceeded'. Workaround: wait one minute.
records.instructions:
1. Failing-first tests. (a) Add server/services/ai-gateway/__tests__/org-cost-cap.test.ts: with a weekly_usage_limits row {metric:'cost_cents', weeklyLimit: 100, overageCapPct: 0, enabled: true} for org 7 and api_usage_logs already at 100 cents, gateway.route() under inTenant('7') must reject before dispatch (stubDispatch records no call), in production even when the limits query throws. Show it FAILS at HEAD. (b) Add a test that two GatewayPolicyEngine instances sharing one store share one org bucket (it fails with today's Map).
2. Cost and token cap inside the gateway, not route middleware. In server/services/ai-gateway/gateway.ts route(), after applyOrgPlacementDefaults/refuseUnboundInProduction (around line 1394) and before policyEngine.evaluate, call checkWeeklyLimit(orgId, 'cost_cents', 0) and checkWeeklyLimit(orgId, 'tokens', 0) from server/services/weekly-usage-limits.ts:254 for the bound org (auditOrganizationId). If either is not allowed, throw a new terminal QuotaExceededError (subclass GatewayPolicyError) and write a refusal ledger row via logRefusalRow. If the check throws: fail closed in production (isProductionEnv), fail open elsewhere. Add the same check to the embedding path (around line 1666).
3. Per-plan defaults (founder decides the numbers). Seed default cost_cents and tokens rows per plan through a migration in C2C_MIGRATION_FILES: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING plus a row-count assertion (Rule 1 seed corollary), or resolve defaults in code from the org's plan when no row exists. An org with no row must still get a ceiling in production.
4. Shared rate buckets. Terraform has no Redis, so either (a) provision ElastiCache in terraform/stack and back checkRateLimit (policy.ts:541-580) with INCR+PEXPIRE on key ai:rl:{rateBucketKey}:{floor(now/60000)}, or (b) without Redis, divide maxRequestsPerMinutePerOrg (gateway.ts:4311) by an AI_RATE_LIMIT_INSTANCE_COUNT env set from var.api_desired_count in terraform/stack/main.tf, and document that it is approximate. Keep the in-memory Map only outside production.
5. In server/bootstrap/register-ai-routes.ts:24 pass { failClosed: process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production' } to enforceWeeklyLimit('requests'). Step 2 covers every other gateway caller centrally, so do not add per-route middleware elsewhere (zero-duplication).
6. Re-run tenant-capacity.test.ts, governance-review.test.ts and the new tests, and show the step-1 tests pass.
All commits go on concept2cure-v2 (Rule 0).
records.acceptance: (a) org-cost-cap.test.ts fails at HEAD and passes after: an org over its cost_cents or tokens cap is refused before dispatch, a ledger row records the refusal, and production fails closed when the limit lookup errors. (b) Two policy-engine instances (simulating two ECS tasks) share one org bucket: the 101st call across both is refused. (c) An org with no configured limit row gets the plan default ceiling in production. (d) tenant-capacity.test.ts and governance-review.test.ts [12] still pass.
records.dependencies: Founder: per-plan token and cost defaults. Infra: Redis/ElastiCache in terraform/stack (or accept the approximate per-instance division).

records.title: Deployment Gmail mailbox and Google Calendar now serve only the organisation named by PLATFORM_INTEGRATIONS_ORGANIZATION_ID; other tenants are refused before the account is reached
records.evidenceAtHead: server/services/integrations/platform-integration-owner.ts:29-47 (new since audit; absent at 92ccdba1): callerOwnsPlatformIntegrations() takes the caller from getTenantScope(), never from tool input. It returns false for any other org, an unscoped call, system scope '0', or no owner configured. correspondence-search.ts:103-111 returns configured:false with notYourIntegrationNote before deps.fetchRecent (Gmail) is called. calendar-event.ts:88-90 does the same before insertAllDayEvent. The other path to the shared calendar, server/src/routes/stability.router.ts (~2940-2946), returns 503 CALENDAR_NOT_YOURS. HubSpot (hubspot-client.ts) is gated the same way. gmailIngestToReg (server/src/services/integrations/gmail.ts:95) has no callers. AnaToolExecutor.ts:4465-4502 routes both tools through these gated modules. Tool output is scanned for indirect prompt injection by default (policy.ts:437-440, AI_GATEWAY_SCAN_ALL_ROLES default on), which limits the residual email-injection channel to the owner org. Command run: npx vitest run correspondence-search.test.ts calendar-event.test.ts platform-integration-owner.test.ts -> 13/13 passed, including the negative cases 'another organisation: told none is connected, and the account is not reached', 'an unscoped call', 'the estate-wide system scope' and 'with no owner named, no organisation reaches them'.
records.fixedBy: 70eeae35d (2026-10-01): server/services/integrations/platform-integration-owner.ts:29-54; correspondence-search.ts:103-111; calendar-event.ts:88-90; server/src/routes/stability.router.ts calendar push owner check; tests in server/services/integrations/__tests__/platform-integration-owner.test.ts
records.severityRationale: Cross-tenant read of the mailbox and cross-tenant calendar writes are closed. The gate fails closed when no owner is named, and the decision is pinned by tests that include the negative cases. Per-tenant connector credentials are a recorded post-launch capability (decision P-8), not a defect.
records.humanTestingNote: Expected behaviour: in any org except the one named by PLATFORM_INTEGRATIONS_ORGANIZATION_ID, AnA's regulatory-mailbox search and calendar-event tools reply that the mailbox or calendar 'is not connected for your organisation', and the stability calendar push returns CALENDAR_NOT_YOURS. To exercise these tools, set PLATFORM_INTEGRATIONS_ORGANIZATION_ID to the tester's org id along with GMAIL_OAUTH_JSON / GOOGLE_CALENDAR_ID + GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT.
